title: Government's Response to State Coroner's Suggestions to Mitigate Psychological Effects for Young People under Police Investigation
what_it_is: Government's Response to State Coroner's Suggestions to Mitigate Psychological Effects for Young People under Police Investigation

sections.label: Committee review of young persons
sections.summary: A committee led by the Ministry of Home Affairs reviewed investigation processes for young persons and will implement measures in schools by February 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The committee is led by the Ministry of Home Affairs and includes the Ministry of Social and Family Development and the Attorney-General's Chambers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As announced by the Minister for Home Affairs last week, the committee has undertaken a comprehensive review of the investigation processes for young persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Following the recommendations, we will implement further measures that will provide enhanced support for the well-being of young persons under Police investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: These measures will be implemented in schools by February 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Any young person conveyed from one of our schools to the Police station for an interview will generally be accompanied by an appointed school personnel familiar to the young person.

sections.label: Appropriate Adult scheme for young suspects
sections.summary: The review committee recommended an Appropriate Adult scheme to give emotional support and observe young suspects for psychological distress during law enforcement interviews.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The review committee has also recommended the implementation of an Appropriate Adult (AA) scheme for young suspects, as announced by the Minister for Home Affairs last week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This Appropriate Adult will provide emotional support and observe the young person for signs of psychological distress during the interview by law enforcement agencies.

sections.label: Appropriate Adult neutrality in investigations
sections.summary: The Review Committee said an Appropriate Adult is more suitable because the person in attendance in a Police investigation should be neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: According to the Review Committee, an Appropriate Adult is more suitable because in a Police investigation, the person in attendance should be neutral.
